In [6]:
# calculate IQR bounds

iqr_bounds = {}

for col in anomaly_columns:
    
    Q1 = df[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = df[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    
    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    
    iqr_bounds[col] = {
        "Q1": Q1,
        "Q3": Q3,
        "IQR": IQR,
        "Lower_Bound": lower_bound,
        "Upper_Bound": upper_bound
    }

iqr_summary = pd.DataFrame(iqr_bounds).T

print("IQR Anomaly Detection Bounds")
display(iqr_summary.round(2))

In [7]:
# create anomaly flags

for col in anomaly_columns:
    
    Q1 = df[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = df[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    
    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    
    flag_name = f"{col}_Anomaly"
    
    df[flag_name] = (
        (df[col] < lower_bound) |
        (df[col] > upper_bound)
    )

print("Anomaly Flags Created Successfully")

print("\nAnomaly Counts:")
for col in anomaly_columns:
    flag_name = f"{col}_Anomaly"
    print(f"{flag_name:<30}: {df[flag_name].sum()}")

Anomaly Flags Created Successfully

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 10))

plot_columns = [
    ("Units_Sold", "Units Sold Anomalies"),

    ("Forecast_Error", "Forecast Error Anomalies")
]

for ax, (col, title) in zip(axes.flat, plot_columns):
    
    flag = f"{col}_Anomaly"
    
    normal_data = df.loc[~df[flag], col]

        range(len(normal_data)),

        s=8,
        alpha=0.35,
        label="Normal"

    ax.scatter(

        anomaly_data,
        s=18,
        alpha=0.8,
        label="Anomaly"
    )
    
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xlabel("Observations", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel(col, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", labelsize=10)
    
    for label in ax.get_xticklabels() + ax.get_yticklabels():
        label.set_fontweight("bold")
    
    ax.legend()

# create z-score anomaly flags

z_threshold = 3

for col in zscore_columns:
    z_col = f"{col}_ZScore"
    flag_col = f"{col}_Z_Anomaly"
    
    df[flag_col] = df[z_col].abs() > z_threshold

print("\nZ-Score Anomaly Counts:")

for col in zscore_columns:

In [11]:
# compare IQR and Z-score anomalies

comparison_data = []

for col in anomaly_columns:
    
    iqr_flag = f"{col}_Anomaly"
    z_flag = f"{col}_Z_Anomaly"
    
    iqr_count = df[iqr_flag].sum()
    z_count = df[z_flag].sum()
    
    both_count = (df[iqr_flag] & df[z_flag]).sum()
    iqr_only = (df[iqr_flag] & ~df[z_flag]).sum()
    z_only = (~df[iqr_flag] & df[z_flag]).sum()
    
    comparison_data.append([
        col,
        iqr_count,
        z_count,
        both_count,
        iqr_only,
        z_only
    ])

anomaly_comparison = pd.DataFrame(
    comparison_data,
    columns=[
        "Feature",
        "IQR_Anomalies",
        "ZScore_Anomalies",
        "Detected_By_Both",
        "IQR_Only",
        "ZScore_Only"
    ]
)

print("IQR vs Z-Score Anomaly Comparison")

display(anomaly_comparison)

In [12]:
# create combined anomaly score

iqr_flags = [f"{col}_Anomaly" for col in anomaly_columns]
z_flags = [f"{col}_Z_Anomaly" for col in anomaly_columns]

df["IQR_Anomaly_Count"] = df[iqr_flags].sum(axis=1)
df["ZScore_Anomaly_Count"] = df[z_flags].sum(axis=1)

df["Combined_Anomaly_Score"] = (
    df["IQR_Anomaly_Count"] +
    df["ZScore_Anomaly_Count"]
)

df["Confirmed_Anomaly"] = df["Combined_Anomaly_Score"] >= 2

print("Combined Anomaly Detection Completed")

print("\nCombined Anomaly Score Distribution:")
display(
    df["Combined_Anomaly_Score"]
    .value_counts()
    .sort_index()
)

print(
    "\nConfirmed Anomalies :",
    df["Confirmed_Anomaly"].sum()
)

print(
    "Normal Observations :",
    (~df["Confirmed_Anomaly"]).sum()
)

Anomaly Detection – Business Interpretation¶

The anomaly detection analysis identified 396 confirmed anomalies from the feature-engineered supply chain dataset using a combination of IQR and Z-Score statistical methods.

Key Findings¶

  • Forecast Error was the leading anomaly driver with 229 flagged observations, indicating significant gaps between actual demand and forecasted demand.
  • Demand Forecast contributed 137 anomaly signals, highlighting unusual forecast behavior.
  • Units Sold contributed 109 anomaly signals, indicating unusual demand patterns.
  • Inventory Level contributed 6 anomaly signals, showing relatively fewer extreme inventory observations.

Anomaly Severity¶

The combined anomaly score identified:

  • 295 observations with Score 2
  • 21 observations with Score 3
  • 79 observations with Score 4
  • 1 observation with Score 5

Higher scores indicate stronger anomaly evidence across multiple detection criteria.

Operational Insights¶

  • SKU_29 recorded the highest number of confirmed anomalies with 17 cases.
  • WH_2 recorded the highest warehouse-level anomaly count with 92 cases.
  • North recorded the highest regional anomaly count with 104 cases.
  • 2024-03-25 recorded the highest daily anomaly count with 7 cases.

Business Relevance¶

These anomalies can help supply chain teams identify unusual demand patterns, forecast inaccuracies, inventory irregularities, and locations requiring further investigation. The detected anomalies should be treated as investigation alerts rather than automatically removed records, because genuine business events can also appear as statistical anomalies.
